preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line) <= 20 for line in stdin.splitlines()[0].split())
preconditions.description: The first line contains two positive integers A and B (1 ≤ A, B ≤ 20) representing the picture dimensions.
The input consists of exactly A + 1 lines: the first line with A and B, followed by A lines of B uppercase letters each.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line) == B for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: Each of the A subsequent lines contains exactly B uppercase English letters.
For any valid X and Y, X must divide A and Y must divide B (X, Y are integers).

postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is a positive integer representing the number of valid (X, Y) pairs where the puzzle is good (no two pieces are identical under rotation).
The output consists of exactly two lines.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= A for x in stdout.splitlines()[1].split()) and all(1 <= int(y) <= B for y in stdout.splitlines()[1].split())
postconditions.description: The second line contains two integers X and Y (1 ≤ X ≤ A, 1 ≤ Y ≤ B) representing the minimal piece size (smallest area XY, then smallest X) among all good puzzles.

postconditions.expression: all(X * Y <= A * B for X, Y in [(int(x), int(y)) for x, y in [stdout.splitlines()[1].split()]] + [(int(x), int(y)) for x, y in [stdout.splitlines()[0].split()]] if len(stdout.splitlines()[0].split()) == 2])
postconditions.description: The minimal piece size (X, Y) is chosen such that its area XY is minimized, and if there are ties, the smallest X is chosen.

postconditions.expression: all(X % A == 0 and Y % B == 0 for X, Y in [(int(x), int(y)) for x, y in [stdout.splitlines()[1].split()]] + [(int(x), int(y)) for x, y in [stdout.splitlines()[0].split()]] if len(stdout.splitlines()[0].split()) == 2])
postconditions.description: The minimal piece size (X, Y) must satisfy X divides A and Y divides B.

postconditions.expression: all(unique_pieces(X, Y, picture) for X, Y in [(int(x), int(y)) for x, y in [stdout.splitlines()[1].split()]] + [(int(x), int(y)) for x, y in [stdout.splitlines()[0].split()]] if len(stdout.splitlines()[0].split()) == 2])
postconditions.description: For every valid (X, Y) pair in the output, the puzzle is good, meaning no two pieces are identical under rotation (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°).

invariants.description: A helper function to check if all pieces in the puzzle are unique under rotation. The picture is divided into X × Y pieces, and each piece is compared to its rotations (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°). The canonical form is the lexicographically smallest rotation.
